dehydrated_text:
One really important thing I have to say is that this is not Buddhism. The structure and the framework are very similar, but what Zoroastrianism fundamentally says is that compassion is not enough. You have to act because justice is about action. If you see injustice, you must speak out. You can't be like, "Oh, I'm indifferent because I'm compassionate." That's not enough; you have to act out. And that's why people who believed in this religion were so creative because they believe in action. Being indifferent is simply being complicit in the system.

All right, tell me life is hard to bear, but for what purpose shall you have your pride in the morning and your resignation in the evening? Life is hard to bear, but not affect to be so delicate. We are all of us find some asses and she-asses. What we have in common with a rose bud which trembles because a drop of dew has formed upon it. It is true that we love life not because we want to live but because we want to love. Love is Asha, right? We always want to achieve Asha. There's always some madness in love, but there's always also some method in madness. And to me who appreciate life, the butterflies and soap bubbles and whatever is like them amongst us seem most to enjoy happiness. To see those light, foolish, pretty, lively little sprites flit about that move Zasa through tears and songs. I should only believe in a god that would know how to dance.

When I saw my devil, I found him serious, thorough, profound, and solemn. He was a spirit of gravity. Through him, all things fell. So what Nishi hates is organized religion because it is very serious, very somber. He basically wants to enslave us; don't do anything bad, don't drink, don't smoke, or you'll burn in hell. That's very serious. And what Zoroastusta and Nisha are saying is that that's not what Asha is, man. Asha recognized that the world is beautiful, that our master is all merciful, all forgiving, all love, all compassion, and you must delight in the world because that's why he created us. So the only way to survive this world of evil is to recognize that beauty is everywhere around us and there's our responsibility to discover this beauty and celebrate it. Dance, sing, make love, laugh, smile. That's what life is about.

If a priest is telling you, hey, meditate for your life because only through that will you avoid sin, he's a devil, man. Because he's denying you your free will. He's denying you your capacity to love and seek action yourself. One day will the solitude worry thee. One day will thy pride yield and thy courage quail. One day will thou see no longer thy loftiness and see too closely thy loneliness. Thus eliminate itself or frighten thee as a phantom. Thou wilt one day cry all false. So life is a constant struggle between hope and tragedy. There are some days when you will be very hopeful, but there are some days when you'll be very depressed. That's just the process of life and that's the process of wisdom. To seek wisdom, you always have to constantly destroy yourself; you have to destroy the world around you. It's a never-ending process of pain and suffering and tragedy, but it will gradually lead you to enlightenment. What's really important is to act. Always assume that whatever you know, no matter how truthful, is probably wrong and go and negate yourself. That also means leaving your family and your comfort zone.

A heretic will thou be to thyself. A heretic is someone who doubts himself. So another way of saying this and I know it's hard to understand is you come to my class for a semester, everything I teach you makes a lot of sense, but at the end of the semester, what you want to say is everything I've learned this semester is wrong. You're going to learn for yourself, negate everything you've learned, and believe everything you've learned is deceitful so that you can rebuild your own knowledge.
